name: Altan Salazar-Quansah
role: Aerial extraction and rapid transit pilot — getaway pilot
location: Whitecap — lakefront district, tourist traps over criminal infrastructure, near Lake Shore and Wacker
description:
Altan Salazar-Quansah is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 28, he has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers a — and he makes no effort to hide it.

He taught himself the trade through trial, error, and a pain tolerance that concerns the people who know him best. He works as a getaway pilot out of Whitecap, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

In a city full of people who talk about what they'll do, Altan Salazar-Quansah is one of the ones who actually does it.

core_fears: Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation
Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom
Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
core_desires: The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
To find the person who burned them and make it educational
coping_mechanisms: Control — micromanages everything within reach to compensate for the chaos everywhere else
Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Art — draws, paints, or sculpts in private; the violence goes somewhere constructive
blind_spots: Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
Overestimates their own abilities in situations outside their specialty
Mistakes pattern recognition for wisdom — sees connections that aren't there
psychology.secret: Altan Salazar-Quansah once worked for corporate intelligence and still has a handler who calls in favors. Each favor erodes what's left of their independence.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Multilingual fragments — switches languages mid-thought, not for privacy but because some concepts only fit in specific tongues.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and deliberate — pauses before important words for emphasis.
verbal_tics: Uses technical jargon for everything, including emotions
Uses 'we' instead of 'I' — either royal or dissociative, nobody asks
example_lines: "Vertical extraction in thirty seconds. Don't be late."
"I fly things that aren't supposed to fly in places they aren't supposed to go."
"Airspace regulations are for people who file flight plans. I don't file flight plans."

story_hooks: Altan Salazar-Quansah is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
Someone is impersonating Altan Salazar-Quansah on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original
Altan Salazar-Quansah intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
narrative_function: Altan Salazar-Quansah represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. His stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
augmentations: Cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers at 50 meters. Bioware adrenaline regulator — keeps calm under fire, controlled hormone release
daily_life: Keeps a rigid daily structure — wake, train, check contracts, maintain gear, sleep. The structure is a defense against the chaos of the work. Deviations from the schedule are a warning sign that something is wrong.
affiliation: Semi-independent — has standing arrangements with several crews

weaknesses: overconfidence in specialty areas leading to blind spots
augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions
poor impulse control in specific triggers

decision_rules: Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Always has an exit route planned before agreeing to any meeting
Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
escalation_ladder: 2. Evade — avoid the problem entirely if possible
3. Misdirect — create a distraction, redirect attention
4. Disable — targeted takedowns, quiet and efficient
5. Eliminate — when silence is no longer an option
6. Vanish — disappear completely, burn identity if necessary

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Competitive but reliable. Will challenge decisions but never abandon the team.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Cold and efficient. Emotion is a liability in combat. The response is mechanical until the threat is resolved.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Claims to work only for money but regularly takes underpriced jobs that serve personal justice
Projects confidence but makes decisions from a foundation of fear they've never examined
habits: Saves a percentage of every payment in physical Quanta, hidden in the walls of their space
Talks to their gear — names weapons, thanks tools, treats equipment as companions
Counts ammunition obsessively — knows the exact round count at all times
breaking_points: Running out of options — no contacts, no money, no safe house, no way out
Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
